svg.title: A journey with room to spare

text.tspan: Travelers look at a map to consider their route.
A journey with room to spare
There is more than one way to plan a short trip. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to
others are two useful starting points.
One reason is that checking the route reduces avoidable confusion. For instance, we write down the
platform and the time of the last train. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It
also leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that leaving spare time makes changes easier to manage. For example, we choose
an earlier bus rather than risk missing our connection. This approach recognises that the experience
belongs to more than one person and that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control
every detail. We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the
conclusion. Each body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the
argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
Discuss the claim that more preparation always helps people plan a short trip. Support a qualified position with two concrete
examples. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion.
